I fixed the double count and committed it as `e76e914` on `main`.

**The cause:** `run_nightly_job` in `src/orders-service-v1/nightly_job.py` counted payment rows. A bank retry adds a second row with the same payment id, so it was counted twice.

**The fix:** the job now collects the ids of unmatched payments into a set and returns its size, so each payment id counts once. I also added a regression test, `test_bank_retry_with_same_payment_id_is_counted_once`, which fails on the old code.

**Tests:** all 9 tests pass with `python3 -m unittest`.

**Not committed:** your uncommitted `README.md` edit and the untracked `notes/` directory. The commit touches only the job and its test.

**Possible follow-up:** `src/orders-api/reconciliation_worker.py` has the same row-counting logic and a "runs once a night" docstring. If that worker also feeds the nightly numbers, it will double-count retries too. I left it alone because you named the nightly job specifically. Say if you want the same fix there.
